item.title: Sqwod Daily · Friday, 06 November 2026
item.description: Today's issue covers HOTWORX's 913-location growth strategy, Strong Pilates doubling its UK footprint, and new research on older-adult fitness variation from Germany.
item.content:encoded:
Friday, 06 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Friday, 06 November 2026 · Weekday
HOTWORX reaches 913 locations on a simplicity model, Strong Pilates targets 20 UK studios in 2027 & DSSV flags wide fitness variation in adults 60–75
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Today's issue covers HOTWORX's 913-location growth strategy, Strong Pilates doubling its UK footprint, and new research on older-adult fitness variation from Germany.
Sqwod
 
5 jobs this week
Fitnesstrainer/in at av Fitness UG (haftungsbeschränkt), Erkner, €20,000–€30,000 / year
Physiotherapeut in Voll- und Teilzeit (m/w/d) at Athera Unternehmensberatung GmbH & Co. KG, Bad Aibling, €20–€30 / hour
Physiotherapeut in Voll- und Teilzeit (m/w/d) at Athera Unternehmensberatung GmbH & Co. KG, Bremen, €20–€30 / hour
Physiotherapeut in Voll- und Teilzeit (m/w/d) at Athera Unternehmensberatung GmbH & Co. KG, Düsseldorf, €20–€30 / hour
Ausbildung Sport- und Fitnesskaufmann/-frau (m/w/d) (IST) at MEDA Sportakademie GmbH, Groß Nordende, €10,800–€13,200 / year
See all jobs →
 
Connect the dots
How HOTWORX built 913 locations by keeping operations simple
Stephen Smith, founder and CEO of HOTWORX, appeared on the Club Solutions podcast with editor Taylor Gabhart to explain the approach behind his infrared fitness franchise's growth to 913 locations. Smith credited a recurring monthly dues model, which he said has anchored fitness business models for more than 30 years by smoothing cash flow, and a philosophy he calls 'more workout, less time', which shortens session length to save members time and money. He described disciplined control of staffing, technology and programming complexity as the repeatable engine behind the brand's expansion, with 1,000 locations now in sight.
For operators and coaches weighing what to add, Smith's account is a direct argument that restricting complexity is itself a growth strategy. Keeping the member promise narrow and the labour model lean means each new location replicates the same proven system rather than inheriting the problems of a more elaborate operation.
 
The rundown
01
DSSV study finds wide variation in fitness potential among adults aged 60–75
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, released a study on 5 November 2026 at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin examining adults aged 60 to 75, known as Generation Ü. The study found this age group holds significant potential for continued work and social participation, but that health, social connection, and individual motivation vary considerably within it. For studio operators and coaches, the findings point to the risk of treating older adults as a single segment and suggest that programming for this demographic needs to account for wide differences in capacity and motivation.
Source: DSSV →
02
HOTWORX CEO Stephen Smith outlines how simplicity drives 913-location growth
Stephen Smith, founder and CEO of HOTWORX, appeared on the Club Solutions podcast with editor Taylor Gabhart to explain how keeping operations simple, staffing lean and the member promise clear has driven the infrared fitness brand to 913 locations, with 1,000 in sight. Smith credited the recurring monthly dues model, which he said has anchored fitness business models for more than 30 years by smoothing cash flow, and a 'more workout, less time' philosophy that reduces session length to save members both time and money. For operators weighing how much technology and programming to add, Smith's account is a direct argument that restricting complexity is itself a growth strategy.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
Strong Pilates targets 20 new UK studios in 2027 after doubling its footprint in 2026
The Australian-born boutique fitness franchise opened seven UK studios in 2026, bringing its total to 15 locations, up from eight at the end of 2025. Confirmed sites include Nine Elms in early 2027, with franchisees exploring West Hampstead, St Albans, White City and Richmond. The pace of expansion signals strong franchisee demand in the UK market, particularly across London and the South East.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Punjab offers free online UPSC and PCS exam coaching to 1,000 students
The Punjab government announced free online coaching for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination and Punjab Civil Services (PCS) examinations, targeting 1,000 college students across the state. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced the initiative, with 750 of the 1,000 seats reserved. The programme is aimed at students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.
Source: The Times of India →
05
fitness MANAGEMENT publishes new edition of medical fitness and healthcare
fitness MANAGEMENT released a new edition of its medical fitness and healthcare magazine, known as mfhc, on 6 November 2026. The mfhc is a twice-yearly specialist publication covering sports medicine, diabetology, rehabilitation, prevention and nutrition, distributed to fitness and health facilities in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, as well as industry companies, congresses and trade fairs. For operators and coaches working at the intersection of fitness and healthcare, the publication is a channel to stay current on clinical and preventive topics relevant to medically oriented facilities.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
 
Policy watch
DSSV study: adults 60–75 vary widely in fitness capacity and motivation
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, released a study on 5 November 2026 at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin showing that health, social connection and motivation differ considerably within the 60-to-75 age group. For studio operators and coaches, the findings point to the risk of treating older adults as a single segment and suggest that programming for this demographic needs to account for wide differences in capacity and motivation.
 
Stat
15
Strong Pilates UK studio locations as of late 2026, up from 8 at end of 2025
Strong Pilates nearly doubled its UK footprint in 2026 and is targeting 20 new studios there in 2027, signalling strong franchisee demand in London and the South East.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 05 November 2026
item.description: VersaClimber passed majority ownership to two of its own executives, while an Indian fitness aggregator closed its first funding round and Germany's annual fitness census opened for submissions.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 05 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 05 November 2026 · Weekday
VersaClimber ownership shifts to Schieffer & Siegrist, OBSESS raises $316K & DSSV launches 2027 German fitness survey
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
VersaClimber passed majority ownership to two of its own executives, while an Indian fitness aggregator closed its first funding round and Germany's annual fitness census opened for submissions.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
OBSESS
 $316K
angel round closed 2 November 2026, backed by Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel and Harshit Vij, eight months after the platform's March 2026 launch
 
The rundown
01
VersaClimber executives Schieffer and Siegrist become majority owners
Shane Schieffer and Jim Siegrist, who have led strategy and sales at VersaClimber respectively, became majority owners of the Santa Ana, California-based equipment brand on 4 November 2026. Schieffer takes the role of chief executive and Siegrist becomes president and chief revenue officer, while the founding Charnitski family retains a minority stake after 45 years of ownership. Studio operators who stock or program VersaClimber equipment can expect continued investment in product development and partnerships, given Siegrist's existing relationships with brands such as Lagree Fitness and TRX.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
02
DSSV launches 2027 German fitness industry data survey
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, Deloitte, and the Deutsche Hochschule für Prävention und Gesundheitsmanagement (DHfPG), a German university specialising in prevention and health management, launched their annual data collection for the Eckdaten der deutschen Fitnesswirtschaft 2027 study on 4 November 2026, calling on all fitness and health facility operators in Germany to participate. The most recent figures show the German fitness sector recorded 12.36 million members, 9,647 facilities, and total revenue of 6.25 billion euros in 2025. Operators facing high running costs, staff shortages, and regulatory pressure stand to benefit from the benchmark data the study produces, which has tracked German market trends annually since 1989.
Source: DSSV →
03
OBSESS raises $316K angel round to connect India's fitness market
Noida-based fitness platform OBSESS closed an angel round of approximately Rs 3 crore ($316K) on 2 November 2026, about eight months after its March 2026 launch. The round was backed by Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel, and Harshit Vij, with proceeds earmarked for partnerships, ecosystem expansion, and technology. OBSESS connects users with gyms, sports facilities, trainers, nutrition services, and fitness products on a single platform, signalling early investor appetite for aggregator models in India's fragmented fitness market.
Source: Dealroom →
 
Policy watch
DSSV opens 2027 German fitness industry data survey
On 4 November 2026, the DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, Deloitte, and the DHfPG, a German university specialising in prevention and health management, launched data collection for their annual Eckdaten der deutschen Fitnesswirtschaft 2027 study, calling on all German fitness and health facility operators to submit data. The study has tracked German market conditions annually since 1989, and its benchmark figures help operators make decisions on costs, staffing and regulatory compliance.
 
Stat
6.25 billion euros
total revenue of the German fitness sector in 2025
Germany's fitness and health club industry generated 6.25 billion euros in 2025 across 9,647 facilities and 12.36 million members, underscoring its scale even as operators contend with high running costs, staff shortages and regulatory pressure.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Wednesday, 04 November 2026
item.description: Arcana's new multi-studio membership hits New York City, Kimberly-Clark completes its Kenvue acquisition, and a London hotel integrates medical care with fitness.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 04 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 04 November 2026 · Weekday
Arcana launches NYC multi-studio membership at $325/month, Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal & St Clement hotel merges medical and fitness
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Arcana's new multi-studio membership hits New York City, Kimberly-Clark completes its Kenvue acquisition, and a London hotel integrates medical care with fitness.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Kimberly-Clark

Connect the dots
Arcana's multi-studio membership model launches in New York City
Arcana launched in New York City with more than 10 boutique studios on its network. Members pay $325 a month for nine classes plus wellness perks, booked through a single account. Partner studios include Reforming Pilates, The Training Lab, Nrthrn Strong, Sui Yoga, ID Hot Yoga, Güdsport, Nofar Method, The Silhouette Method, Good Day Pilates, Elahni, Serotonin Club, Powered on Bond, First Class Form and Outershed. Co-founders Felicia Dodge, who worked in analytics at Twitter and Visa and holds a master's in applied analytics from Columbia University, and Cole Tomlinson, a former mobile software engineer at Wayfair and Trello, started the company after working as yoga instructors and finding it difficult to train across multiple studios.
For studio operators, Arcana represents a multi-studio access product, similar to a network pass, that positions itself as protecting partner revenue rather than undercutting it. Studios already on the network gain exposure to members who might not have found them otherwise, while the $325 price point sits firmly in the premium tier, which may help avoid the margin pressure that lower-cost aggregators can create.
 
The rundown
01
Arcana Launches NYC Multi-Studio Membership Starting at $325 a Month
Arcana, a new premium fitness membership, launched in New York City with more than 10 boutique studios on its network, offering subscribers nine classes a month plus wellness perks from a single account. Co-founders Felicia Dodge, who brings a background in analytics at Twitter and Visa, and Cole Tomlinson, a former mobile software engineer at Wayfair and Trello, started the company after working as yoga instructors and finding it difficult to train across multiple studios. For studio operators, the model signals growing demand for multi-studio access products that aim to protect partner revenue rather than commoditise it.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal to build wellness portfolio
Kimberly-Clark completed its $48.7 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of Kenvue on 3 November 2026, uniting 10 billion-dollar brands across personal care, consumer health, women's health, and active aging. The combined company projects approximately $2.1 billion in run-rate synergies from cost savings and revenue growth. For brands and investors in the wellness and personal care space, the deal signals that large consumer goods companies are consolidating around health and wellness at scale, which may reshape supplier relationships and competitive dynamics for smaller operators in those categories.
Source: Personal Care Insights →
03
St Clement hotel in London combines medical, fitness and wellness under one roof
The Health Club at St Clement, the new London hotel from Soho House founder Nick Jones located at 180 The Thames, has launched with medical services, fitness and wellness integrated together, with Cleveland Clinic among its named collaborators. The pairing of a recognised medical institution with a hospitality-led fitness offer signals growing operator appetite for clinical credibility as a differentiator in the premium wellness market.
Source: Health Club Management →
 
Stat
$2.1 billion
projected run-rate synergies from the Kimberly-Clark and Kenvue combination
The scale of expected savings and revenue gains from this single deal illustrates how aggressively large consumer health companies are pursuing consolidation in the wellness space.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Tuesday, 03 November 2026
item.description: Equinox has a new CEO and a $1 billion growth commitment, while 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov is building a $10 million flagship club in Las Vegas.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 03 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Tuesday, 03 November 2026 · Weekday
Equinox names Brendan Whitworth CEO with $1B growth plan & Mark Mastrov opens $10M Las Vegas club in 2027
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Equinox has a new CEO and a $1 billion growth commitment, while 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov is building a $10 million flagship club in Las Vegas.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Equinox
 $1B
planned growth investment announced alongside new CEO appointment
 
Connect the dots
Equinox installs new CEO and signals $1 billion in growth spending
Equinox appointed Brendan Whitworth as chief executive officer, replacing Harvey Spevak, who led the company since 1999 and moves to the chairman role. Whitworth joins from Anheuser-Busch, where he was also CEO, and will sit on the Equinox board. The company operates 118 clubs across 18 major markets and reported double-digit revenue growth, with membership numbers and check-ins at all-time highs. The transition comes as Equinox plans $1 billion in growth investment.
For studio and gym operators, the Equinox numbers confirm that premium, full-service clubs are still drawing members and capital. If your positioning competes on experience and results rather than price, the data supports holding that ground and investing in the quality signals that justify a premium membership fee.
 
The rundown
01
Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth CEO, Plans $1B in Growth Investment
Equinox appointed Brendan Whitworth as chief executive officer, replacing Harvey Spevak, who led the company since 1999 and moves to chairman. Whitworth joins from Anheuser-Busch, where he served as CEO, and will also sit on the Equinox board. The company reported double-digit revenue growth across its 118 clubs in 18 major markets, with membership numbers and check-ins at all-time highs, signalling that premium fitness continues to attract both capital and consumers.
Source: Club Solutions →
02
24 Hour Fitness founder opens $10M Founders Club in Las Vegas in early 2027
Mark Mastrov, who founded 24 Hour Fitness in 1983, will open Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness in early 2027 at 9200 West Sahara Avenue in Summerlin, Las Vegas. The new facility covers more than 45,000 square feet and represents a $10 million investment, including more than $1 million in recovery equipment, with 25,000 square feet dedicated to free weights and strength training across 12 platforms. The scale of the recovery investment signals that operators building full-service clubs are treating recovery infrastructure as a core offering rather than an add-on.
Source: Club Solutions →
 
Stat
25,000 sq ft
floor space dedicated to free weights and strength training at Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness
Dedicating more than half of a 45,000-square-foot facility to free weights and strength across 12 platforms shows how central strength training has become to the full-service club offer.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Monday, 02 November 2026
item.description: Fund 1 Investments is exploring a bid to take Xponential Fitness private, while Whoop signs LeBron James and Chuze Fitness rolls out Reformer Pilates studios.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 02 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 02 November 2026 · Weekday
Fund 1 bids to take Xponential private, Whoop signs LeBron James & Chuze adds Reformer Pilates
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Fund 1 Investments is exploring a bid to take Xponential Fitness private, while Whoop signs LeBron James and Chuze Fitness rolls out Reformer Pilates studios.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Fund 1 Investments LLC
third-largest Xponential Fitness shareholder is exploring a bid to take the company private
 
The rundown
01
Sekonda launches £79.99 subscription-free smart ring
British watch brand Sekonda expanded its wearable technology range with a smart ring priced at £79.99, requiring no ongoing subscription, to track health and wellbeing around the clock. The no-subscription model may be a useful talking point for operators and coaches recommending wearables to cost-conscious clients.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
Chuze Fitness adds Reformer Pilates studios for MAX members
Chuze Fitness launched Reformer Pilates studios in select locations, offering FreeMotion Reform RX-S reformers in purpose-built spaces with no per-class fees for MAX members. The hybrid model splits each studio between instructor-led group classes and self-guided sessions using on-demand video kiosks, backed by more than 300 iFIT-powered classes at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. For operators considering Reformer Pilates, the model points to one way to address the instructor shortage and equipment intimidation that have kept the format out of mainstream gym environments.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
James Hird joins AI sports data firm backed by Paul Little
Essendon AFL football legend James Hird has put his coaching ambitions on hold to join an artificial intelligence software firm backed by billionaire Paul Little, which targets the commercial sports data market. Hird's move followed the appointment of former teammate Mark McVeigh as Essendon senior coach in August, after a public campaign to install Hird in that role did not succeed.
Source: AFR →
04
Whoop signs LeBron James as global ambassador with 3.5 million members
Health and fitness tracker Whoop signed NBA star LeBron James as its newest global ambassador, the company announced on 29 October 2026. James first wore a Whoop in 2015 as one of its first 100 members, and will now appear in multimedia ad campaigns for the brand, which has 3.5 million active paying members. For fitness brands and investors, the deal signals that wearable companies are investing in high-profile athlete partnerships as they build consumer scale ahead of a potential public offering.
Source: Sportico.com →
05
Fund 1 Investments Pushes to Take Xponential Fitness Private
Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., is seeking to take the company private and is exploring a bid to buy it outright, according to people familiar with the matter. Xponential Fitness owns the Club Pilates brand among other boutique fitness franchises. A successful take-private would remove Xponential from public markets, which could affect how its franchise partners, competitors and suppliers engage with the company going forward.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Stat
3.5 million
Whoop active paying members at the time of the LeBron James signing
The figure shows the scale Whoop has reached as a subscription wearable brand, providing context for why a high-profile ambassador deal with LeBron James makes commercial sense at this stage.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Sunday, 01 November 2026
item.description: Mark Mastrov launched Founders Club, a venue combining strength training, recovery, medical spa and social space, pointing to where premium fitness is heading.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday, 01 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Sunday, 01 November 2026 · Weekday
Founders Club launches as all-in-one training and medical wellness concept, Runna data shows 52% of Gen Z want to marathon but 7% act & Stryv raises $11.5M
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Mark Mastrov launched Founders Club, a venue combining strength training, recovery, medical spa and social space, pointing to where premium fitness is heading.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Stryv
 US$11.5M
Series B led by ACV Capital, with Openspace Capital and OCTAVE Capital, closed October 27 2026, to fund expansion into Taiwan and growth in Malaysia and Hong Kong
 
The rundown
01
Kyle Scheele named second-day keynote speaker at HFA Show 2027
The Health and Fitness Association announced on October 30, 2026 that Kyle Scheele will deliver the second-day keynote, titled "Rethinking What's Possible," at The HFA Show 2027, running March 10–12 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. Scheele, known for large-scale creative projects, will address how organisations can challenge conventional thinking and turn constraints into opportunities. The keynote is sponsored by Matrix Fitness.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
02
Mark Mastrov unveils Founders Club, a fitness, recovery and medical spa concept
24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov has launched Founders Club, a new wellness concept that combines strength training, recovery facilities, a medical spa, and spaces for working and socialising. The concept signals operator interest in bundling training, recovery and medical wellness under one roof.
Source: Health Club Management →
03
Stryv raises US$11.5M Series B to push deeper into Asian wellness hardware
Singapore-based Stryv, a personal care and home wellness brand owned by Evo Commerce, closed an US$11.5 million Series B round on October 27, 2026, led by ACV Capital with participation from Openspace Capital and OCTAVE Capital. The company sells hair dryers, styling tools, massage chairs and air purifiers, and will use the funds to enter Taiwan and expand in Malaysia and Hong Kong, alongside research and development and potential acquisitions. The raise signals growing investor appetite for consumer wellness hardware in Southeast and East Asia, a category that increasingly overlaps with the recovery and self-care products fitness operators stock and recommend.
Source: Alvinology →
04
NYC Marathon valued at $339m as top races become major brands
The New York City Marathon carried a valuation of $339 million as of late October 2026, with major races in London, Paris and Chicago seeing similar increases in value. The figures signal that large running events have grown into significant commercial properties. For fitness brands and studio operators targeting runners, the scale of these events points to growing sponsorship and partnership opportunities in the running category.
Source: Athletech News →
05
52% of Gen Z want to run a marathon but only 7% commit, Runna data shows
New data from running app Runna, published October 30 2026, found nearly a third of Americans and 52% of Gen Z aspire to run a marathon, yet just 7% have committed to a race or physical challenge. Almost half of respondents said they do not consider themselves runners, and a third doubted their fitness level. Run club and event participation fell year on year as costs rose, a signal that operators and brands pricing or positioning running as exclusive risk shrinking the market they depend on.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Stat
7%
share of Americans who have committed to a race or physical challenge, per Runna data published October 30 2026
Despite 52% of Gen Z saying they want to run a marathon, only 7% have made a commitment, and run club participation fell year on year as costs rose, meaning studios and brands that lower the price and perceived barrier to entry have the largest addressable pool of new participants.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Friday, 30 October 2026
item.description: Providence Equity Partners agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, adding a second affordable fitness brand to its European portfolio alongside VivaGym.
item.content:encoded:
Friday, 30 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Friday, 30 October 2026 · Weekday
Providence acquires Fitness Park, Fitness First opens HYROX club in Hamburg & Ozlo raises $22M for sleep tech
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Providence Equity Partners agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, adding a second affordable fitness brand to its European portfolio alongside VivaGym.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Ozlo
 $22M
Series B raised to expand sleep technology products and target new conditions including tinnitus and epilepsy
⇄  Acquired
Providence Equity Partners / Fitness Park Group
Providence agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, adding it to a European affordable fitness portfolio that already includes VivaGym
 
Connect the dots
Providence bets again on affordable fitness in Europe
Providence Equity Partners agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, a budget-focused gym chain. Providence already holds an investment in VivaGym, another affordable fitness operator in Europe. The deal adds a second affordable brand to the firm's European portfolio and continues a pattern of consolidation in the low-cost gym segment across the continent.
For gym operators and brands selling into the affordable fitness category, the deal is a signal that private equity sees further scale and margin opportunity in budget gyms across Europe. Operators in that segment should expect continued competitive pressure as consolidated groups gain purchasing power and marketing reach.
 
The rundown
01
Providence Equity Partners agrees to acquire Fitness Park Group
Providence Equity Partners has agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, adding the affordable fitness brand to its European portfolio. Providence already holds an investment in VivaGym, another affordable fitness operator in Europe. The move signals continued consolidation in the affordable fitness segment across Europe, which operators and brands in that category should watch.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
Orangetheory and Crunch Fitness use wearables to personalise coaching and retention
Club Solutions reported on 29 October 2026 that Orangetheory Fitness and Crunch Fitness have made fitness tracking technology a core part of how members engage with workouts and measure progress. Both brands use wearable data to give members real-time feedback and to give their teams additional tools to support member goals. Operators in the sector can observe that integrating member-generated fitness data into coaching workflows is being used as a direct retention strategy by two large gym chains.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
Ozlo raises $22M Series B to expand sleep tech and target new conditions
Sleeptech company Ozlo raised $22M in Series B funding to advance its products and target new sleep-related conditions, including tinnitus and epilepsy. Ozlo's Sleepbuds combine ergonomic design with Bose audio technology to mask nighttime noise, and the company has passed 200,000 customers through partnerships with Calm and Dreem Health. For fitness and wellness operators, the raise signals growing consumer demand for science-backed sleep tools, a category that is moving beyond passive aids toward biosensing and AI-driven solutions.
Source: Fitt Insider →
04
Fitness First reopens Hamburg club as dedicated HYROX Training Club
Fitness First reopened its club in the Hamburger Stadthöfe on 28 October 2026 under the name Fitness First HYROX Training Club, reorienting the site entirely around functional performance training. The concept combines guided HYROX classes, open gym time, and a recovery area that includes a sauna. The move signals that established gym operators are building dedicated facilities around HYROX as the sport draws a growing global participant base.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
05
aktivpark padel club opens in Kall with courts now bookable
The aktivpark padel club in Kall, Germany, held an opening weekend of training sessions, a Landesliga tournament organised by the Deutscher Padel Verband (DPV, Germany's national padel federation), and an Americano tournament. The club opened with three doubles courts and one singles court, all AFP Panoramacourts by Adidas and available to book online. Padel combines elements of tennis and squash and is played on a court enclosed by glass and mesh walls, which are part of play.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →

Intake Breathing lands $62M to push magnetic nasal dilator into retail
Jim Castillo, a medical device engineer, invented a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tab system that mechanically opens the nasal valve to improve airflow. His son-in-law Alex Hauck runs the company as CEO. Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, has put $62 million into Intake Breathing, marking the brand's first significant outside capital. The funding will take the family-run business into mainstream retail.
For coaches and studio owners building recovery or sleep programming, the raise signals that breathing and recovery products are attracting serious consumer brand investment. As Intake moves into retail, members will encounter the brand outside the gym, which gives coaches an opening to address nasal breathing and airflow as part of their recovery conversations.
 
The rundown
01
$62M Backs Intake Breathing's Magnetic Nasal Strip Expansion
Intake Breathing has raised $62 million from Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, to grow its magnetic nasal dilator brand into mainstream retail. Intake, founded by medical device engineer Jim Castillo and run by CEO Alex Hauck, makes a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tab system that mechanically opens the nasal valve to improve airflow, unlike traditional adhesive strips. The raise signals that sleep, recovery and breathing performance products are attracting serious consumer brand investment, a category relevant to studios and coaches building recovery or sleep programming.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Garmin fitness revenue rises 16% to $694m in Q3 2026
Garmin reported third-quarter fitness segment revenue of $694 million, up 16% year over year, for the quarter ended September 26, 2026, with operating income of $231 million and a 33% operating margin. In July, the company launched the Cirqa Smart Band, a screenless wearable priced at $199.99 with no subscription fee, targeting the same recovery and wellness tracking market as Whoop. For studio and gym operators evaluating wearable partnerships or member-facing technology, Garmin's subscription-free model is a direct contrast to Whoop's paid membership structure and may influence member purchasing decisions.
Source: Athletech News →

Ozwell Fitness tripled recovery service usage after consolidating wellness under one roof
Gemi Ozdemir opened Ozwell Fitness in Carmel, Indiana, combining red light therapy, personal training, sauna and other recovery services in a single facility, using Neo Science wellness technology. The club attracted thousands of new members and tripled usage rates for some recovery services, with Ozdemir reporting strong retention. For operators, the results suggest that bundling recovery and training in one location can drive both engagement and member loyalty.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Lawler and Diaper: value, innovation and human connection drive operator success
Total Fitness CEO Sophie Lawler and Fitness First CEO Marc Diaper told the HCM Summit that delivering value, investing in innovation and protecting human connection are central to fitness operators' success. The two chief executives spoke at the event, according to Health Club Management.
Source: Health Club Management →

Garmin's fitness segment, its largest by revenue, grew 16% year over year with a 33% operating margin, and its new $199.99 screenless Cirqa Smart Band carries no subscription fee, a direct contrast to Whoop's paid membership model that may shape how members choose wearables.

The rundown
01
Mark Mastrov to enter HFA Hall of Fame at March 2027 Las Vegas show
The Health & Fitness Association will induct 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov into its Hall of Fame on March 10 at The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Mastrov built 24 Hour Fitness from a single California gym into a global fitness company, then spent decades founding, investing in, and mentoring businesses across fitness, sports, and wellness. He recently returned as an owner of 24 Hour Fitness, more than 40 years after founding it.

Whoop valued at $10.1 billion
Wearable fitness tracker company Whoop has reached a valuation of $10.1 billion.

Philip Donnay named GLL CEO as Peter Bundey retires
GLL has appointed Philip Donnay as CEO and Andy Bindon as deputy CEO. The appointments follow the retirement of Peter Bundey.
Source: Health Club Management →

BODY20 repositions its EMS model around strength training for women
BODY20, a 20-minute whole-body electrical muscle stimulation franchise, says it is targeting women seeking strength and muscle preservation rather than weight loss. About two-thirds of its members are women, most aged 35 to 55 or older, and director of fitness Sydney Maddox says member conversations have shifted away from calorie burning toward joint health, bone health and long-term capability. For studio operators, the trend suggests that marketing resistance training around longevity and muscle preservation, rather than weight loss, may better match what this demographic now wants.

German studio software provider medo.check has outlined eight principles for what it calls future-ready studio management software, published in trade magazine body Life. The principles cover customisation to individual studio workflows, system integration to avoid isolated data stores, a branded member app, and AI-assisted training monitoring through its medo.core product, while the company says its support line is staffed by people rather than automated tools. Medo.check positions the package around more than 20 years of experience in training management and member care, which may give studio operators a reference point when evaluating whether a software platform can handle both administration and coaching support in one system.
Source: body LIFE →

With roughly two-thirds of its member base being women, most aged 35 to 55 or older, BODY20's data gives studio operators a concrete indication of who is currently drawn to short-format electrical muscle stimulation sessions.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Monday, 26 October 2026
item.description: PureGym acquires Switzerland's NonStop Gym for £235 million, plus new data on member churn and a case for investing in general manager hiring.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 26 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 26 October 2026 · Weekday
PureGym buys NonStop Gym for £235m, Mariana Tek churn signals & Good Soul Hunting on GM hiring
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
PureGym acquires Switzerland's NonStop Gym for £235 million, plus new data on member churn and a case for investing in general manager hiring.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
PureGym / NonStop Gym
 £235 million
PureGym acquires 47-location Swiss low-cost chain NonStop Gym, deal expected to close 2 November 2026
 
Connect the dots
Member churn signals appear months before cancellation
Data from Mariana Tek, a studio management software platform, shows measurable changes in member behavior three to eight months before a cancellation or downgrade. Among members who eventually canceled, average monthly visits fell from 6.2 to 5.4 in the final month before cancellation, and monthly spend dropped 11%. Julie Sippy, director of marketing at Mariana Tek, said the membership change is often the end of a slow, subtle disengagement trajectory, not the beginning of one. The challenge for studios is that disengaging members may still attend classes and generate revenue, giving no obvious sign that they are at risk.
For studio operators, this means a member who looks active on a roster may already be drifting. Tracking visit frequency and spend trends over rolling months, rather than checking current membership status alone, gives studios a larger window to reach out and strengthen engagement before a cancellation decision is made.
 
The rundown
01
Mariana Tek: Member churn signals appear 3–8 months before cancellation
Data from Mariana Tek, a studio management software platform, shows measurable changes in member behavior three to eight months before a cancellation or downgrade. Among members who eventually canceled, average monthly visits fell from 6.2 to 5.4 in the final month before cancellation, and monthly spend dropped 11%. Studio operators who track visit frequency and spend trends over time may be able to identify at-risk members while there is still time to act.
Source: Athletech News →
02
PureGym buys Swiss chain NonStop Gym for £235 million
PureGym is acquiring NonStop Gym, a low-cost gym chain with 47 locations in Switzerland, for £235 million. The deal is expected to close on 2 November 2026, after which NonStop Gym sites will be rebranded as PureGym, giving the combined network more than 100 Swiss locations by end of 2026. The acquisition follows PureGym's purchase of Blink Fitness in the United States in 2024, and will make PureGym the largest low-cost gym operator in Switzerland.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Global Wellness Institute flags EMFs as an unaddressed factor in built environments
The Global Wellness Institute published an article stating that electromagnetic fields (EMFs) are present in almost every indoor space but are rarely considered in design decisions. Citing research from the Building Biology Institute, the article links elevated EMF exposure to changes in sleep, nervous system activity, cognitive fatigue, and melatonin regulation. Studio and gym operators who are already designing around light, air quality, and natural materials may find EMF exposure a relevant next consideration for their environments.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
04
J Potter Community Fitness raises £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now in one-week challenge
J Potter Community Fitness, based in Worcester, ran The Big Pink Journey from 14 to 21 October, with 100 supporters walking, dancing and exercising a combined 776 miles to raise £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now. The original targets were £1,500 and 315 miles. The campaign shows that a clearly defined distance goal and a one-week window can help small fitness communities significantly exceed fundraising targets.
Source: The Worcester News →
05
ViralSpoon joins DSSV as a supporting member
ViralSpoon, an AI social media management tool, has joined the DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, as a supporting member, announced on 21 October 2026. The tool connects to Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn and uses artificial intelligence to plan, create and publish posts automatically, matching a studio's existing visual style and tone. Studio operators running multiple locations can manage all accounts from a single dashboard, with campaigns adapted by the AI for each site so platforms do not flag them as duplicate content.
Source: DSSV →
06
Good Soul Hunting applies executive search methods to boutique fitness GM hiring
Good Soul Hunting, a fitness industry recruitment firm, is positioning the general manager role as a direct growth lever for boutique fitness operators. Co-founder and managing partner Matt Adey said a strong general manager or studio manager is responsible for turning a brand's vision into measurable results at the local level. For studio operators, the hire who runs the floor has more direct impact on member experience than any strategy set at head office.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Stat
3 to 8 months
how far in advance churn signals appear before a member cancels or downgrades, according to Mariana Tek data
Studios that monitor visit frequency and spend trends have a window of several months to identify at-risk members and act before a cancellation is made.

Orangetheory Fitness launched OTconnect for Apple Watch on October 23 at participating U.S. studios, letting members pair their own Apple Watch to the brand's in-studio performance-tracking platform for a one-time $99 connection fee. During class, members can see heart rate, heart rate zones, calories burned and Splat Points on their wrist, and review a performance summary in the Orangetheory app afterward. Club Studio, the premium group fitness concept from Fitness International, the parent company of LA Fitness, plans to open clubs at 8484 Wilshire Boulevard in Beverly Hills and 2001 Wilshire Boulevard in Santa Monica. The Santa Monica site will be its second in that city. No opening dates have been announced. The expansion shows continued appetite for concepts that combine boutique group fitness, strength and cardio equipment, personal training, and recovery services under one roof, a model studio owners in competitive urban markets may want to monitor.

JOHN REED opens first Stuttgart location at over 2,200 sq m
JOHN REED opened its first Fitness Music Club in Stuttgart, Germany, on 23 October 2026. The club, at Arnulf-Klett-Platz 1 near the main railway station, covers more than 2,200 square metres and includes cardio and strength equipment, a 110-square-metre functional training area, milon X machines, 12 Reformer Pilates benches from Your Reformer, planned regular HYROX classes, two saunas, a rest area, and a coffee and health bar.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →

WILDE, a US maker of chips and crackers derived from chicken breast, egg whites, and bone broth, secured $40 million from investor S2G Investments on 22 October 2026 to expand retail distribution and launch new products. The company already sells in more than 30,000 retailers and recorded over $100 million in sales last year, and is opening a 130,000-square-foot facility that will increase production capacity sixfold. Coaches who sell or recommend snacks to clients may find high-protein whole-food options like these easier to position as consumer demand for protein-rich foods continues to grow.
